chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a house containing multiple dwellings where they share one path within the courtyard. If one of them sold his house to a man, do his partners have the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) in the path? He said: 'If the door of the house and what surrounds it faces the path, and otherwise it does not, then they have no right of pre-emption. But if he sold the path along with the house, then they have the right of pre-emption.'

key_terms.الشُّفْعَةُ: Right of pre-emption (the right of a partner or co-owner to buy out another's share before an outsider)
key_terms.عَرْصَةِ الدَّارِ: The courtyard or open space of the house

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for exercising the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) in a shared pathway?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the conditions for *shuf'ah* (pre-emption) in shared real estate, distinguishing between exclusive access paths and general thoroughfares. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on preventing harm (*darar*) and ensuring equitable usage rights among co-owners, a principle deeply rooted in the Prophetic tradition of protecting neighbors' interests.
